chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from Sayf ibn 'Umayra, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abi al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

O Ibn 'Ammar! Do not leave the recitation of the Surah 'Tabarak alladhi nazzal al-furqan 'ala 'abdihi', for whoever recites it every night, Allah will never chastise him, nor will He call him to account, and his abode will be in the highest Garden of Paradise.

key_terms.الْفِرْدَوْسِ الْأَعْلَى: The highest level of Paradise, often considered the dwelling place of the prophets and the most righteous.
key_terms.تَبَارَكَ الَّذِي نَزَّلَ الْفُرْقَانَ: The opening phrase of Surah al-Furqan (Chapter 25 of the Quran), often used as a title for the Surah.
key_terms.لَمْ يُحَاسِبْهُ: He will not be called to account (muhasabah), implying a lighter or easier reckoning on the Day of Judgment.
key_terms.لَمْ يُعَذِّبْهُ: He will not be punished (adhab), indicating protection from divine chastisement.

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for reciting Surah al-Furqan every night according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) emphasizes the spiritual efficacy of nightly recitation of Surah al-Furqan, linking it to exemption from punishment and strict accountability (*hisab*). This practice is particularly significant in Shia tradition as a means of securing a permanent abode in *Al-Firdaws al-A'la*, the highest tier of Paradise, reflecting the Surah’s thematic focus on divine authority and the Quran as the criterion of truth.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. From the previous chain from al-Hassan from Sayf b. ’Umayra from Ishaq b. Ammar from Abi al-Hassan (a.s.) who said: “

O Ibne Ammar! Do not avoid recitation of Tabaarakalladhee nazzalal furqaana a’laa a’bdihi. One who recites it every night, Allah will never chastise him and not take his account and his abode will be in the high garden of Paradise.”
